item.title: Russian Drone Hits Romania, Iran Deal Pending, China Nuclear Build
item.description: A Russian drone struck a residential block in NATO member Romania, injuring civilians for the first time. Meanwhile a tentative 60-day US-Iran ceasefire extension awaits approval, newly revealed satellite imagery shows China hardening its nuclear second-strike infrastructure at massive scale, and Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket destroyed its only launch pad in Florida.

item.title: Iran Ceasefire Fractures, Oman Threatened
item.description: The US-Iran ceasefire is under severe stress after overnight exchanges near the Strait of Hormuz and Trump's threat to bomb American ally Oman. Also: CSIS quantifies the multi-year Pacific vulnerability created by Operation Epic Fury munitions depletion, adversaries are exploiting commercial location data to target US troops, and Israel strikes Beirut for the first time since the mid-April Lebanon ceasefire.

item.title: Iran Ceasefire Fractures as Draft Hormuz Deal Emerges
item.description: U.S. strikes on Iran during active ceasefire negotiations contradict simultaneous diplomatic signals, as a draft deal to reopen Hormuz shipping surfaces. Israel escalates in Lebanon, Taiwan's arms package is formally paused, and South Korea commits to nuclear submarines.

item.title: Iran Ceasefire Under Fire, NATO Commitments Cut
item.description: US strikes Iran during Doha peace talks, Netanyahu intensifies Lebanon bombardment, and Washington formally reduces the fighter jets and bombers it will provide NATO in a crisis — the week's compounding signals of US retrenchment.

item.title: Iran Formalizes Hormuz Control as Negotiations Stall on Two Fronts
item.description: Iran establishes a formal authority over the Strait of Hormuz and hardens its nuclear position, as both Ukraine and Russia grow skeptical of U.S. mediation and China advances its AI governance agenda at the UN.

item.title: Russia Nuclear Drill, NATO Autonomous Zone, Salt Typhoon Doctrine
item.description: Russia launches its largest unannounced nuclear exercise in years, NATO operationalizes autonomous-systems doctrine on its eastern flank, and China's Salt Typhoon campaign signals a fundamental shift toward data-centric intelligence advantage. Plus: Taiwan's $14B arms deal hangs in uncertainty after Trump's Beijing summit.

item.title: NATO Retrenchment, Estonia Drone Shootdown, and the Putin-Xi Summit
item.description: The Trump administration formally notifies NATO allies of reduced U.S. force commitments as Europe confronts a Romanian F-16 shootdown of a Ukrainian drone over Estonia and Reuters reports China covertly trained Russian forces fighting in Ukraine. The Senate advances a War Powers Resolution on Iran with rare Republican support.

item.title: Iran Talks Stall, Flotilla Intercepted Again, Ebola Emergency
item.description: Pakistan mediates Iran war negotiations as Trump escalates threats and delivers a second flotilla interception near Cyprus; WHO declares an Ebola emergency as six Americans are evacuated from DR Congo.

item.title: Beijing Summit Readout Gap and the Iran Arsenal Dispute
item.description: Trump and Xi leave Beijing with sharply divergent accounts of what was said about Taiwan, while a classified intelligence leak and CENTCOM testimony offer contradictory pictures of how much of Iran's military survived the U.S. bombing campaign.

item.title: Japan Fires from Philippine Soil, Pentagon Plans Mass Missiles
item.description: Japan fires anti-ship missiles from the Philippines for the first time since World War Two, activating First Island Chain deterrence as the Pentagon announces ten thousand low-cost cruise missiles. The Strait of Hormuz remains selectively open for Chinese vessels as Trump meets Xi in Beijing.

item.title: Hormuz Escalation, Ceasefire Theater, and the Chokepoint Template
item.description: US and Iran exchange fire in the Strait of Hormuz as Navy F/A-18s disable tankers with smokestack bombs; Ukraine's counter-drone expertise reshapes global security architecture while a fourth ceasefire cycle collapses ahead of Victory Day.

item.title: Hormuz Deal or War, Ukraine Ceasefire Collapse, China AI
item.description: The US-Iran ceasefire memorandum reaches a 48-hour deadline as France deploys its carrier to the Red Sea; Ukraine's Victory Day ceasefire collapses for the third straight cycle; China's open-source AI models are gaining global market share while the West watches benchmarks.

item.title: Iran deal signal, Ukraine ceasefire failure, Pakistan submarine
item.description: Oil markets moved on reports of a potential US-Iran framework deal even as Iran continued striking UAE targets and Hormuz shipping; Russia rejected Ukraine's unilateral ceasefire with drone attacks; Pakistan commissioned its first Chinese submarine, reshaping South Asian naval balance.

item.title: Ukraine's Air Defense Hangs on Iran
item.description: The U.S. war in Iran is creating direct resource competition for Patriot interceptors Ukraine depends on, while Israel commits to a $118 billion military build, Indian elections reshape the national opposition, and European leaders convene on Russian-aligned Armenian soil.
